facts.text: Tyro’s name comes from the English word meaning beginner or novice today.
Tyro Mill, built 1846‑47 by William Massie, showcases Oliver Evans‑style automated grinding machinery for corn, wheat, and rye in the heart of the town today and still operational.
Crabtree Falls, just north of Tyro, drops over 1,200 feet, the tallest cascading waterfall east of the Mississippi in Virginia and draws nature enthusiasts year round for its spectacular view.
Tyro suffered severe flash flooding during Hurricane Camille in 1969, reshaping its river valley landscape for future development.
Tyro sits in Nelson County’s Tye River valley, about 30 miles south of Charlottesville and 25 miles northeast of Lynchburg providing access to urban via State Route 56.
Tyro’s bedrock consists of metamorphosed Lynchburg Group sandstones, siltstones, and conglomerates, overlaid by alluvial deposits that shape local soils for agricultural use.
